sections.h2: Which Garrard County office answers which tax question
sections.html:
Value is the PVA's job and the bill is the sheriff's. The PVA does not set rates or collect money, and the sheriff does not assess property, so an argument over the figure goes to one office and a question about paying goes to the other.

Both offices are at 319 Stanford St. in Lancaster. Call the PVA at (859) 792-3291 on weekdays between 8 and 4, or the sheriff at (859) 792-3591. The PVA is a state-supervised office with a local address, and its valuation standard is full fair cash value on each January 1.

Twenty-eight taxing districts are collected by the sheriff, covering state and county levies, school districts, and special districts for fire protection, libraries and similar services. Each October 1 the bills go out with instructions on due dates, penalties, mortgage-company payment and ways to pay. The County Clerk, at 15 Public Square, Suite 5, records deeds and helps notify and collect on delinquent bills.

sections.h2: Garrard County housing and the local market
sections.html:
East-central Kentucky holds Garrard County, mostly rolling Bluegrass farmland, with the Knobs in the southeast corner near Cartersville. Lancaster is the seat and only city, about 28 miles south of Lexington, and the average commute runs 33.1 minutes. Every resident was classed as rural in 2020.

  • Population: 18,207 in the 2025 estimate, up 7.4 percent from 2020.
  • Typical home value: $204,900 in the 2020 to 2024 survey.
  • Homes lived in by their owners: 79.9 percent.
  • New-home permits in 2025: 0.
  • Rent runs a median $794 gross, and household income a median $63,087.

In 2020 there were 7,254 housing units, 9.2 percent of them empty, and 6,584 households. No permits were recorded in 2025, so sales are mostly existing houses and acreage. Buyers of older farmhouses and acreage often ask about the tax record early, so keep last year's receipt and this year's bill together in one folder for showings and for the closing agent.

sections.h2: Due dates and the early-payment discount
sections.html:
The bill is mailed October 1 and falls due December 31, so the discount window lasts about a month. Under KRS 134.015, a bill settled in full by November 1 drops 2 percent. A January payment carries 5 percent extra, and each payment after that carries 10 percent.

If mailing runs late statewide, Revenue can swap in a short calendar of a month with the discount, a month at face, then a month with the 5 percent charge. The January 1 owner is personally liable for that year's tax, so a closing early in the year needs a clear agreement about the bill.

Come April 15 the sheriff hands off unpaid bills to the County Clerk, and a lien goes on record against the parcel. Penalties and commissions stack up quickly from there, and each step adds cost for whoever owns the parcel.

How an open Garrard County bill moves through the year
WhenWhat happens to the bill
October 1Sheriff mails the bill
Through November 1Full payment earns the 2 percent discount
November 2 to December 31Face amount is due
JanuaryAn extra 5 percent applies
After JanuaryAn extra 10 percent applies
April 15County Clerk receives the bill and records a lien
Weeks after transferInterest, county attorney letters, then the clerk's sale 90 to 135 days after transfer

Interest builds at 1 percent monthly. A 30-day notice and a second notice come from the county attorney. When a certificate sells to an outside buyer, you owe that buyer plus its additional fees.

Make the tax bill part of the sale paperwork. The sheriff mails bills in October, and the debt belongs to the January 1 owner, so a house that closes in spring or summer may still have a bill outstanding in the seller's name.

  • Phone the sheriff's office at (859) 792-3591 for the amount due on the parcel.
  • Ask the County Clerk at (859) 792-3071 how to record the deed, since the clerk's office archives deeds and mortgages.
  • Tell the PVA at (859) 792-3291 who the new owner is so later notices and any exemption follow the right person.
  • Keep the paid receipt with your closing file, because the buyer's title search will otherwise show the balance as open.

Owners who are behind on taxes and facing repairs on an older farmhouse may weigh a direct sale to a buyer that closes as-is. That route avoids carrying the bill through a long listing. With cash there is no lender appraisal or repair list, and the tax payoff is taken from the price at closing. Get the payoff figure in writing so the title company has a firm number.

Once a Garrard County house is under contract, the title company hunts for open taxes at the sheriff and the clerk. A paid current bill is settled by a receipt. An open one is listed on the settlement statement and paid from the seller's proceeds. If the bill slipped past April 15, the lien sits in the clerk's records, and the title company will want the clerk's payoff instead of the sheriff's.

The timing of your sale decides who is on the hook. A sale before the October 1 mailing leaves the current year's bill to be split in the contract, because it will arrive in the seller's name for the January 1 ownership. A sale after the bill is mailed is simpler: pay the sheriff and file the receipt. Either way, give the PVA the buyer's mailing address after closing so notices stop coming to you.

Start with a PVA conference. After that, file your appeal at the County Clerk's office. Viewing of the roll runs 13 days from early May. The clerk wants the appeal by the next business day after that ends.

A local review board meets roughly four to five weeks after that. It decides on documents such as comparable listings, construction costs and photographs, and it must put its reasons for any change in writing. A paid representative has to be an attorney, appraiser or another approved professional and must carry your written authorization.

For 2025 and 2026, seniors and totally disabled owners lose $49,100 from the assessed value used for the bill. The PVA on Stanford Street takes the application.

A birth certificate, license or passport shows your age. A seller who has held the exemption should tell the PVA after closing so it ends at that address. The buyer then files a fresh application if they qualify. Lancaster staff at the PVA can tell you what documents to bring, and applying early in the year avoids a gap on the next bill.

faqs.q: When do Garrard County tax bills go out?
faqs.a: On October 1 each year. Anyone who pays the entire bill by November 1 saves 2 percent.

faqs.q: Who should I call if a Garrard County tax value looks wrong?
faqs.a: Call the Garrard County PVA at (859) 792-3291. The sheriff's office never assesses value and refers those questions to the PVA.

faqs.q: Where is the Garrard County sheriff's tax office?
faqs.a: Go to 319 Stanford St. in Lancaster, KY 40444, or phone (859) 792-3591. The sheriff collects for 28 taxing districts.

faqs.q: What changes for Garrard County taxes still open on April 15?
faqs.a: The County Clerk receives it as a certificate of delinquency and records a lien. Interest builds monthly, and clerk and attorney commissions follow.

faqs.q: What is the Garrard County homestead exemption worth?
faqs.a: It lowers assessed value by $49,100 for 2025 and 2026 on a home owned by a senior or a totally disabled person.
